best_idea: A map drag that is a click unless the pointer moves past a pixel tolerance or holds past a time window, that moves the view by accumulated motion, and that undoes the step (not clamps the view) at the map edge.
decision_why: Keep the sticky pixel dead zone plus short-press window with restore on click, the accumulated grab-style offset, and the rollback at the limits; reject the OS cursor warp and virtual cursor, which a browser cannot do without pointer lock and touch does not need. The donor's rollback branches drop the window scale that the normal path applies; the sketch uses one mapping for both.
acceptance: A quick tap (under 300 ms and under 10 px of motion) does not pan the map and runs the tap action (centre on the tapped point); a press that moves past 10 px pans the map with the pointer; at the zone edge the pan stops with no jump on the next move.
